title: Improving Education in Young Offender Institutions

speakers.name: Jake Richards
speakers.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Justice

contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Justice (Jake Richards)
contributions.text: The primary mission of youth custody is to turn around the lives of those children who arrive in our care, while protecting the public. This means a focus on rehabilitative services that really work, leading to reduced reoffending upon release and better outcomes for our communities. High-quality education in custody is central to that mission. It gives children the skills, qualifications and confidence to progress into training or employment. These are the foundations of successful integration back into the community, and each child has a right to high-quality education that sets them up for life, whether in the community or in youth custody. That is why earlier this year I commissioned the Children’s Commissioner for England, Dame Rachel de Souza, to review education services in youth custody, to understand why the current education offer is too often failing to meet the needs of children in custody, and to identify the reforms needed to improve outcomes. This builds on the vision set out by our youth justice White Paper, “Cutting Youth Crime.
